templates.name: Investors
templates.headline: built, updated from Dycom's Nov 11 review
templates.pagesServed: investors/ and the investor content pages: stock, governance, committees, analyst coverage, shareholder services, FAQs

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body:
The interior frame the whole site inherits, and the investor's front door. Since Nov 16, 2026 it also serves the investor content pages — stock information, governance, board committees, analyst coverage, shareholder services and FAQs — with the same kit (rich text, data table, accordion, document list, Investor resources); there is no separate investor-content template. An analyst or shareholder arrives after a results release or from the Investors menu.
1. Open on the latest numbers.
2. Keep the call replay one click away — and permanently in the menu.
3. Show what's next (Upcoming events) and what was said (news).
4. Reach every investor page once, through Investor resources.
5. Never send the visitor off-site: the IR provider's material renders on-site.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — INVESTORS (updated Nov 16, 2026 from Dycom's Nov 11 review)
notes.body:
Results bar above the header on every page for 14 days after earnings: the release and the call replay.
Hero: company description, NYSE: DY listing block; unnumbered jump row.
Latest financial results, Q2 2027 as a green sub-line: three GAAP figures over photography, the four-document package, the replay in one line.
Brand film band — after the results, so the page opens on the numbers.
Events (Upcoming / Past, split by date) beside Investor news (four latest).
Featured reports.
Investor resources: filings, governance, shareholder resources (News & events dropped — it has its own sections).
Stay informed, then white space before the footer.
Menu: permanent 'Latest results & call replay'.

notes.heading: SITECORE MAPPING (built in the site)
notes.body:
ResultsBar (new, global, header partial design; release date, window and links from one shared item, later the IR feed) · InteriorHero + listing · PageIndex (ShowNumbers off) · SectionHead with sub-line · MetricBand · DocumentList · Statement (replay block) · Video (homepage film item, compact) · SplitSection → EventTimeline (Upcoming/Past, empty state) + ResultList (news) · CoverCards · LinkColumns (reads the Investors navigation columns) · ClosingBand (SpaceAfter).
SiteHeader: SpotlightLink per navigation group.
Figures, events and news → IR feed (D-IR).

notes.heading: OPEN FOR DYCOM
notes.body:
• New hero boilerplate — marked for replacement, no text supplied; the current description stays.
• 'Whole snapshot' with a stock price — live market data from the IR provider conflicts with no outward links / no market widgets; needs a provider and on-site rendering decision.
• Investor resources on every interior investor page — confirmed direction, applied when those templates are built.
Build notes: call transcripts become HTML pages (Notified to supply); gated webcasts expose VideoObject/Event metadata; link-level analytics + Google tag on the governance column.
Results bar is forced on for review (ForceShow) — switch off to follow the 14-day window.

templates.name: Section landing
templates.headline: one template, two sections
templates.pagesServed: Who we are, What we do, Our companies

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body:
A visitor clicked a group's overview link (Who we are, What we do). They have chosen a topic, not a page. The landing must:

1. Confirm where they are (breadcrumb, H1, one-sentence answer).
2. Tell the section's story in a few beats, in Dycom's voice.
3. Route them to every child page — the mega-menu columns, as tiles.
4. Prove it (facts from the one managed source).
5. Close with one next step.

Used by: who-we-are/, what-we-do/ (and companies/ if separated from the directory). Careers gets its own landing (T07).

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — WHO WE ARE
notes.body:
Hero: who Dycom is, in one sentence. Incorporated 1969, NYSE: DY.
01 Purpose: to connect America; the six values, stated once (they repeat on two pages today — audit §7).
02 Explore: the section's pages as tiles, grouped as the menu groups them.
03 How we work: Headway® and Rightway™ — the two programmes in everything Dycom publishes.
04 By the numbers: the facts band, from the Company Facts source.
05 Connection with Intention: the shared block, authored once (ABT0005).
06 News, then one closing step: the company near you.

notes.heading: SITECORE MAPPING
notes.body:
InteriorHero (+ Breadcrumb) · InPageIndex · SectionIntro (new) · ChildPageTiles (new, reads the nav group so menu and tiles never disagree) · FeaturePair (new) · CompanyFacts (shared datasource) · SharedPromo (shared datasource) · NewsList (IR feed) · CtaCallout (new).

New components to build: C02 breadcrumb, C15 tile card, C16 counters, C19 CTA callout.

notes.heading: OPEN FOR DYCOM
notes.body:
• One line per value — the values have names but no published definitions.
• 'Connection with Intention' copy: consolidated here from the repeated block; Dycom to approve the wording.
• Leadership tile links to people pages that need photos and bios (T15).
• Company facts: 20,000+ vs 21,000+, ~40 vs 41 — needs one owner (D-CF).
• Electrical contracting has no service page yet (brief open item 9).
Same template, different section: What we do swaps the purpose block for the lifecycle route and adds 'Who we build for' and a directory teaser (C29) — optional sections switched on in the CMS.

templates.name: Corporate topic
templates.headline: the long-form story page
templates.pagesServed: Values, safety, quality, sustainability, trades, veterans, benefits…

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body:
One topic, told fully: the page a visitor reads, not scans. 19 pages use it — values, operating strengths, safety, quality, sustainability, business segments, the trades, why Dycom, students, veterans, recruitment process, life, benefits, capabilities.

It must:
1. State the topic in one sentence (hero).
2. Let a long page be navigated — the sticky 'On this page' list (C08), numbered sections.
3. Mix the right blocks for the topic from one kit.
4. End in related pages and one next step.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — HEADWAY® SAFETY
notes.body:
The audit names Safety the deepest page on today's site; ABT0003 asks for accordions and in-page anchors.

Hero: what Headway® is, and the one fact that defines it — anyone can stop the work.
01 Safety before schedule — the four commitments.
02 Before work starts — the job-task assessment, as four steps.
03 Training and mentoring — 50/50 media block.
04 Hazard recognition — document list, English and Spanish (RES0004).
05 Stop-work authority — the statement, set large.
06 Safety resources — accordion by audience (CC-7), including 811 for communities.
Related → closing: find open roles.

notes.heading: THE KIT (required → optional)
notes.body:
Required: InteriorHero · TopicNav (sticky, C08) · numbered TopicSection with rich text · Related (C21 related-content) · Closing.

Optional per page: listing block · process steps · 50/50 media (CC-17) · document list (C23) · statement/quote (C09) · accordion (C07) · pillars (shared promo, 3–4 up) · counters (C16) · video (C11) · timeline (C20) · form (C25).

Sustainability shows the light end: no listing block, three sections, a report download.

notes.heading: OPEN FOR DYCOM
notes.body:
• Hazard guide file sizes and dates come from the DAM (RES0005–0006).
• Job-task assessment steps are an Icreon draft — confirm against Headway®.
• Training copy: confirm the mentoring model.
• Sustainability: report year and file; pillars are three (brief) plus Business practices (ABT0004 lists four) — confirm the framing.
• Environment pillar copy is limited to what Dycom has published (site restoration).

templates.name: Service detail
templates.headline: one template, deep and thin
templates.pagesServed: The seven services, then Building Systems

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body:
A customer or candidate wants to know: do you do this work, who does it near me, and can I work in it? Seven services (SVC0001–0005) plus Building Systems later.

SVC0002 sets the stack: introduction · capabilities with icons · media · operating companies providing the service · related projects (optional) · contact · related careers.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — WIRELINE (DEEP)
notes.body:
Hero: what the service is, in Dycom's lifecycle words; listing block places it in the lifecycle (stage 03 of 05) so every service reads as part of one journey.
01 What we build — four capabilities with the brand's own pictograms (CC-11).
02 In the field — the current page's video, migrated, beside how a route gets built.
03 Our wireline companies — the directory pre-filtered to this service (SVC0003, C29).
04 Careers — the trades in this service, a live count from the job feed and a filtered drawer (SVC0004, C30).
Related services → contact.

Project management (thin) switches media, careers and related off — the audit found it thin today.

notes.heading: BLOCKED ON DATA
notes.body:
• Company → service tagging does not exist (D8, SVC0003). The companies module is designed; its rows are marked placeholders until Dycom tags each company.
• Live role count needs the feed's department → trade mapping (C30).
• Pictograms: the brand set has six. Aerial and splicing borrow the closest (antenna, arrows); two new pictograms should be drawn to the same spec.
• Wireline video: migrate the current page's video to the DAM.
• Electrical contracting / Building Systems: taxonomy pending (SVC0005).

templates.name: Company directory
templates.headline: the map as a page
templates.pagesServed: companies/ — the map as a page

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body:
companies/ — the map as a page (MAP0001–MAP0008). A customer, candidate or neighbour wants the company for their area, or one they have heard of.

1. Say what the companies are: local names, one national group.
2. Search by place or name; filter by company, service line, state.
3. Show where they are: the map, with the selected company's card.
4. List every company A–Z — the map's accessible equivalent and its fallback when the map fails or is blocked by consent.
5. One next step.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — OUR COMPANIES
notes.body:
Hero: local employers, one national group; listing block '~40 companies' with Dycom's 'over 500 field offices' line.
01 Find a company: search, filters, result count, Use my location; the Civic map exactly as on the homepage, with the company card open — logo first, home office, website ↗, careers ↗, View open roles. There are no company profile pages: the card and the A–Z rows lead to each company's own website.
02 All companies A–Z: letter index, logo rows, list-works-without-the-map notice.
Closing: not sure which company to call?
Phones: no map (brief rule); a row opens the card as a dialog.

notes.heading: SITECORE MAPPING

InteriorHero (+ listing) · CompanyFinder (search + filters, C35 — reads the Company items) · CompanyMap (the homepage component) with CompanyCard (MAP0002, MAP0004) · CompanyDirectoryGrid (A–Z, logo, list fallback — MAP0006–0008) · CtaCallout.

New: filter bar, A–Z index, logo row, map-failure notice (C38).

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body:
The front door for every candidate. Most don't know Dycom's job titles.
1. Search first: role, then location (C31).
2. Answer 'where do I fit?' in plain-language trades, not SAP department names.
3. Show what working here is like: video, benefits, why Dycom.
4. Earn trust: recruitment-fraud guidance on the page.
5. Never dead-end: the talent network.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — CAREERS
notes.body:
Hero: skilled work with a local employer, search bar, popular searches.
01 Where do I fit? Eight trades, each with a one-line explainer and an open-role count.
02 Life at Dycom: video library filtered by tag (CC-6), led by the brand film.
03 Benefits: in-page slider (CC-13), one slide per category.
04 Why Dycom: local employer, trained on the job, room to grow; Veterans and Students.
05 Apply safely: the fraud notice.
Closing: join the talent network.

Role counts and roles shown come from the sample SuccessFactors-shaped feed, not live vacancies.

templates.name: Job search
templates.headline: role and location first, never a dead end

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body: Search like a job seeker: role and location first, plain-language filters, an honest count, never a dead end. Filters only on facts SuccessFactors supplies as fields: trade (department → trade on the Trade items), company (facility), state, employment type (shifttype), travel, trainee (from the title).

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — FIBER SPLICING IN GEORGIA
notes.body:
Compact Civic band: breadcrumb, 'Open roles', search pre-filled.
Left: filters with counts. Right: result count read to screen readers, sort (recent, nearest), removable chips.
Result cards (C32): title, company logo and name, city/state/ZIP, type, travel, posted, trade tag, trainee tag, pay slot shown only when the feed has pay.
Pagination · talent network · 'Looking for something else?' → site search (NAV0010).
No-results board (C34): says what was searched, maps the word to a trade ('cable splicer' → Fiber splicing), widen the search, nearest similar roles and companies, talent network.
Phone: filters behind 'Filters (2)'.

Roles shown are from the sample feed.

notes.body: Decide with confidence, then apply from a phone. One requisition: the facts a candidate needs, the employer named and linked, a clean hand-off to apply, and fraud guidance where the decision happens.

Similar roles.

templates.name: Resource listing
templates.headline: find one item in a growing archive

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body: Find one item in a growing archive. Used by News, Investor news, Events & presentations and the Resource Center index (RES0001). Search, narrow with filters, see what is filtered, page through, never dead-end.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — INVESTOR NEWS
notes.body:
Hero: what the archive holds; listing block → the latest results (Q2 2027).
Search, then filters (type, topic, year, sort) with removable chips and a live count.
Results: date, title, optional summary, type · topic tag. Pagination.
Zero-result state: say what found nothing, Clear filters, cross-link to SEC filings.
Closing: email alerts or Investor Relations.

templates.name: Article / news detail
templates.headline: read it, trust it, act on it

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body: Read one release or article in full, trust it, act on it. Used by News, Investor news and Resource Center articles (RES0003). Render the feed's text exactly, carry Article structured data (sitemap, llms.txt), keep the documents beside it, lead on to related items.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — Q2 2027 RESULTS RELEASE
notes.body:
Article hero: no photograph; type and date above an H1 sized for long titles.
Dateline and lede, then the three GAAP figures as a strip ($2.006 billion, $115.6 million, $3.81).
Release body, outlook, results call and financial tables come from the IR feed exactly as issued — bracketed here, never retyped.
About Dycom and forward-looking statements.
Sticky aside: the four results documents, IR contact, share (copy link, email, print — nothing leaves the site).
Closing: more investor news.

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body: Get the right official document fast. Seven pages: annual and quarterly reports, SEC filings, governance documents, hazard recognition, employee handbook, benefit plan disclosures. CC-23 asks for 'a more elegant version' of today's annual reports page; RES0004–0006 set what each document shows and require stable DAM URLs.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — ANNUAL REPORTS
notes.body:
Hero: what the library holds; listing block = next fixed date (annual meeting May 28, 2026).
Latest reports: cover cards across years.
Full list: year tabs and document type; each row title, type, size, date, tag; PDFs open in a new tab.
Accessibility route: request another format.
Related financials and filings. Closing: printed copies or contact IR.

Files from the DAM with stable URLs (RES0005); untagged PDFs flagged at upload (RES0006).

notes.heading: THE JOB
notes.body:
The way in for every question that is not a job application. Six pages: contact, subcontractor request, talent network, document request, email alerts, contact IR.
1. Say what it's for; send job seekers to open roles first.
2. Ask who they are, then only what that inquiry needs (FRM0001).
3. Fail kindly: name each fix, keep the values (FRM0006).
4. Confirm where the inquiry went.

notes.heading: NARRATIVE — CONTACT
notes.body:
Hero: Contact Dycom; listing block answers the commonest wrong turn: applications go through open roles.
01 Reach us: headquarters, Investor Relations, suppliers and subcontractors, company directory.
02 Send an inquiry: seven types (FRM0001), open on Customer or project; fields follow the live closing form; consent; quiet bot check (FRM0007).
States board: A validation (summary + per-field fixes, aria-invalid + text) · B sent (route, recap, next step) · C Careers opens the drawer instead of a form · D subcontractor request (FRM0011) on the same engine. Values filled in on the states board are illustrative.

FormPlacement left/right/top/bottom (C25, FRM0005). Variants: subcontractor, talent network, document request, email alerts (C26). CRM push later (FRM0010).
